summary:
Traditional scientific sonifications often map satellite data to cold, robotic sine-wave beeps that quickly cause listener fatigue. EKTRION — The Telekinetic Jukebox transforms NASA Earth and space telemetry into an expressive, human-centered musical instrument. Instead of generating random tones from pixels, Ektrion lets real NASA satellite data sculpt music created from a user’s own voice.
Users hum a short melody into their microphone, shape it into a rich instrumental arrangement using AI, and pass that song through five interactive NASA exploration stages: a 2D Hubble/Earth studio (01 Create), a dual-sphere 3D VideoTexture Earth mixer (02 Globe), a camera-driven full-body silhouette instrument (03 Embodied), a sound-painting satellite turntable featuring Mauritius’s first CubeSat (04 Image Atlas), and a blind acoustic discovery quiz (05 Listening Test).
Ektrion is important because it makes complex planetary datasets—from wildfire carbon monoxide plumes and stratospheric ozone to Southwest Indian Ocean cyclones—intuitively audible, accessible to visually impaired learners, and emotionally memorable for students and the public.
details:
What exactly does it do?

EKTRION — The Telekinetic Jukebox is a five-stage interactive web workstation that turns NASA Earth Information Center (EIC), NASA Scientific Visualization Studio (SVS), NASA Hubble, and Mauritian MIR-SAT1 satellite imagery into playable, real-time musical experiences:

  1. 01 Create (Voice-to-NASA Studio):

    Users hum an 8-second melody into their microphone (Module 01), transform it into an instrumental arrangement via AI (Module 02), and hear NASA imagery sculpt the song’s volume, pitch, filter warmth, and tempo while plucking musical chimes across detected star and storm clusters (Module 03).


  2. 02 Globe (Single & Dual 3D Planetary Mixer)

    Wraps official equirectangular NASA SVS video datasets ( IMERG Cyclones, Ocean Winds, and VIIRS NDVI Vegetation) onto interactive Three.js 3D globes. Users can enable Dual-Globe Mode to DJ-mix and acoustically compare two planetary systems side by side.

  3. 03 Embodied ("Become the Instrument"): Uses real-time webcam computer vision and laser-pointer/hand tracking so a user’s own body silhouette reveals three stacked NASA layers simultaneously: Upper Body (Air / Ozone), Middle Body (Land / Vegetation), and Lower Body (Ocean Currents). Includes Silhouette, Stencil (draw-on-black-canvas), and Flashlight modes, plus Capture Sonic Artifact for social sharing.


  4. 04 Image Atlas (Mauritius MIR-SAT1 Sound-Painting Turntable):

    Takes raw monochrome satellite imagery from Mauritius’s first CubeSat (MIR-SAT1) and NASA MODIS Cyclone Batsirai and uses a sweeping acoustic scanline to dynamically colorize black-and-white telemetry into living tropical reefs, volcanic ridges, and storm bands as the music plays.


  5. 05 Listening Test (Blind Acoustic Discovery):

    Challenges users to first hear a baseline song, then listen to two hidden NASA satellite sonifications (Cyclone Batsirai vs. Rising Galaxies) and identify the physical phenomena purely by ear before revealing the satellite imagery.

How does it work?

At the core of Ektrion is our 60 FPS V4 3-Graph Contour + Canny Small-Object Jukebox Engine built on the HTML5 Canvas and Web Audio API:

  • 3-Graph Spatial Extraction: Every video frame or satellite image is sampled onto an offscreen canvas (1020×430 or 960×540). For every vertical scan column, the algorithm computes three normalized physical signals:
    • Cyan Curve (Intensity & Concentration Mass): Drives master volume envelope, low-shelf bass warmth (130 Hz), and low-pass filter cutoff.
    • Orange Curve (Vertical Center of Gravity / Thermal Latitude): Bends musical pitch in semitones () as storm bands or galactic cores rise and fall.
    • Green Curve (Vertical Spread & Sobel/Canny Edge Turbulence): Modulates playback tempo () and rhythmic LFO tremolo chopping in turbulent regions.
  • Canny Small-Object Music-Box Detector: A connected-component detector over Canny edge gradients identifies isolated features (stars, urban
    hubs, convective storm cells) and triggers stereo-panned pentatonic/Lydian chimes at the exact moment the scanline crosses each feature.
  • Sound-Painting Color Restoration (04 Image Atlas): Maps acoustic energy and pixel luminance gradients across raw monochrome MIR-SAT1 CubeSat frames into multi-stop spectral palettes (coastal reef jade/coral, Mascarene solar glint, and cyclone vortex cyan).

What benefits does it have?

  • Eliminates "Sine-Wave Fatigue": By using real music (and the user's own voice) as the acoustic carrier instead of raw oscillators, listeners stay engaged and immediately notice subtle shifts in pitch, rhythm, and timbre caused by scientific anomalies.
  • Accessibility & Blind Discovery: Visually impaired users and students can perceive spatial structures—such as the calm eye of a Category 4 cyclone vs. its turbulent eyewall, or a rising galactic core—purely through sound, validated directly in our 05 Listening Test.
  • Embodied & Kinesthetic Learning: Students don't just passively watch charts; they use their hands, body posture, and voice to physically "play" Earth's atmosphere, land, and oceans.
  • Restoring Local Space Heritage: Brings monochrome imagery from Mauritius’s first satellite (MIR-SAT1) to life through synchronized acoustic colorization.

What do you hope to achieve?

We aim to deploy EKTRION as both an open web platform (ektrion.app) and an interactive museum/classroom installation in Mauritius and globally—bridging art, accessibility, and Earth science so anyone can hear, feel, and share the pulse of our planet.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project?

  • Languages: TypeScript, JavaScript (ES2022), HTML5, CSS3
  • Frontend Framework & UI: React 19, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Lucide Icons, GSAP (GreenSock Animation Platform), Custom Verlet Physics Patch-Cable Engine
  • 3D Graphics & Spatial Rendering: Three.js (THREE.WebGLRenderer, THREE.VideoTexture, custom atmospheric Fresnel shaders), HTML5 2D Canvas API
  • Audio DSP & Synthesis: Web Audio API (AudioContext, OfflineAudioContext, BiquadFilterNode, StereoPannerNode, DynamicsCompressorNode, AnalyserNode), custom V4 3-Graph & Canny Jukebox DSP engine
  • Computer Vision & Embodied Tracking: MediaPipe Tasks Vision (@mediapipe/tasks-vision Hand Landmarker), custom real-time webcam background-subtraction & 3-strata body segmentation
  • Backend & Music AI Integration: Node.js, Express, tsx, Suno AI API (upload-cover and generate endpoints for vocal-hum-to-arrangement synthesis), ffmpeg (video/audio transcoding), PM2 (production server management)
  • Hardware Used: Standard laptop/desktop webcam and microphone
